status_summary: Executive Order 14265 (signed 2025-04-09, published 2025-04-15) set a commercial-solutions-first preference, ordered a review of major programs more than 15 percent behind schedule or over cost for possible cancellation, and ordered workforce and requirements-process reviews; no public result of that cancellation review was found. On 2025-05-01 the Army announced it would end procurement of the AH-64D, stop buying the HMMWV and JLTV and drop the Gray Eagle drone, and move funding toward capability-based portfolios, which resembles the Mandate's call to end outdated programs. On 2025-11-07 the Defense Secretary issued a memo (dated 2025-11-07 on media.defense.gov) renaming the acquisition system the Warfighting Acquisition System and, per a law-firm summary, directing that major acquisition move into Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) portfolios within two years, with scorecards, removal mechanisms for poor performance, a commercial-first default and 180-day tasks to transform Defense Acquisition University and to produce test-and-evaluation and budget-flexibility recommendations. The Department's Acquisition Transformation Strategy, posted the same week, states plans to give PAEs more freedom to shift funds, to pursue the 2024 PPBE Commission's reforms, to work with Congress on more multiyear procurement, and to rename Defense Acquisition University the Warfighting Acquisition University. The FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60, dated 2025-12-18 on govinfo.gov) lists in its table of contents Sec. 1802 (establishment of the role of portfolio acquisition executive), Sec. 1822 (modifications to commercial products and commercial services), Sec. 804 (multiyear procurement authority for covered systems and certain munitions) and Sec. 825 (report on strengthening the Defense Acquisition University); an industry guide describes them as making the portfolio executive a statutory senior acquisition official, making commercial solutions the starting point, expanding multiyear procurement eligibility and ordering a review of the university. By March 2026 the Navy had set up six PAEs and was transitioning three more. The outputs of the 180-day budget-flexibility and DAU tasks, any enacted PPBE change, and revised Buy America treatment of defense items were not found. The memo itself still could not be opened from the Department's site; a vendor-prepared summary of it and summaries by two law firms and DefenseScoop describe the same two-year PAE transition and 180-day budget-flexibility tasks, and the law firms and DefenseScoop also report a 150-day update of the 5000-series instructions. For FY2027, the House passed its defense authorization bill (H.R. 8800) 216 to 212 on 2026-07-22 (House Clerk roll call 278); a War on the Rocks comparison of the House and Senate texts reports further PAE and multiyear procurement provisions. Cloture on the motion to proceed to the Senate bill (S. 4784) failed 50 to 46 on 2026-07-14, and CRS showed no FY2027 authorization enacted as of 2026-09-01.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14265 (signed 2025-04-09, published 2025-04-15) prefers commercial and other streamlined buying pathways, orders reviews of major defense acquisition programs for possible cancellation and of the joint requirements process, and sets reform-plan deadlines of 60 to 180 days.

Army Secretary and Chief of Staff letter announces the Army Transformation Initiative: end of AH-64D procurement, excess HMMWV and JLTV, and the Gray Eagle drone, a shift from program-based to capability-based portfolios, and a merger of Futures Command and Training and Doctrine Command.

The Defense Secretary issues a memo (dated 2025-11-07) redesignating the acquisition system the Warfighting Acquisition System; the official copy could not be opened. Per summaries by Venable, Covington and DefenseScoop, program executive offices are to be restructured into PAEs with all major acquisition moved within two years, with 90-day commercial-first guidance, a 150-day update of the 5000-series instructions, and 180-day tasks including portfolio scorecards, Defense Acquisition University transformation and budget-flexibility recommendations. A vendor-prepared summary of the memo gives the same structure, says the 5000 series will be updated without naming a deadline, and adds four-year PAE terms.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of War (memo, official copy unreachable); Venable, Covington and DefenseScoop summaries; Carahsoft vendor summary

timeline.event: The Department posts its Acquisition Transformation Strategy (Rebuilding the Arsenal of Freedom; posted date from the media.defense.gov path). It plans to realign some program executive officers as PAEs with more authority over resources and requirements, to give PAEs more freedom to shift funds, to pursue 2024 PPBE Commission reforms, to seek more multiyear procurement from Congress, to reduce dependence on non-allied suppliers, and to rename Defense Acquisition University the Warfighting Acquisition University.
The Navy establishes its first PAE, for robotics and autonomous systems (December 2025; day not given, first of month used).

The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act becomes Public Law 119-60 (S. 1071; date shown on govinfo.gov). Its table of contents lists Sec. 1802 (portfolio acquisition executive), Sec. 1822 (commercial products and services), Sec. 804 (multiyear procurement authority) and Sec. 825 (Defense Acquisition University report); an industry guide published 2025-12-23 describes statutory PAEs, commercial solutions as the starting point, wider multiyear eligibility and a university effectiveness review.

The Navy announces five more PAEs (maritime, undersea, industrial operations, strategic systems, Marine Corps); PAEs take over contract, technical, and sustainment authority from the systems commands (March 2026; day not given, first of month used).

The House passes its FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800), 216 to 212 (roll call 278). A War on the Rocks comparison published 2026-07-16, before passage, reports that the House bill would let PAEs issue performance ratings and shift up to 10 percent of research funds to procurement, and that both bills extend multiyear procurement authority for munitions (13 in the House, 19 in the Senate). Cloture on the motion to proceed to the Senate bill (S. 4784) failed 50 to 46 on 2026-07-14; CRS shows neither bill enacted as of 2026-09-01.
timeline.source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House (roll call 278); U.S. Senate (vote 195); CRS; War on the Rocks

uncertainties: The Secretary's 2025-11-07 acquisition memo (media.defense.gov) returned HTTP 403, so its terms (two-year PAE transition, 90-, 150- and 180-day tasks) come from the Venable summary and DefenseScoop; the Acquisition Transformation Strategy posted with it was read through its first 100,000 characters, and states plans rather than completed actions. The NDAA text itself was seen only through the table of contents on govinfo.gov (Public Law 119-60); the effect of Secs. 804, 825, 1802 and 1822 comes from an industry guide (War on the Rocks), and the page date 2025-12-18 is not labeled as the approval date. The table of contents shows no section on PPBE reform, block buys or a general Buy America change (Sec. 831 concerns the Berry Amendment and seafood only), but the body text was not searched. Not found: whether any program was cancelled through the EO 14265 review (the Army letter does not say), any PPBE reform in practice, or any outcome of the Defense Acquisition University tasks. Month-only events use first-of-month dates. Freshness pass 2026-10-12: the media.defense.gov memo again returned an error, and no Department news release or CRS description of the memo was located. A document hosted by a contractor-services vendor, first taken as a copy of the memo, is a vendor-prepared summary carrying the vendor's copyright and marketing sections, not the memo text; it agrees with the law-firm and press summaries on the two-year transition, the 90-day commercial-first guidance and the 180-day budget tasks, says the 5000 series will be updated without giving a deadline, and alone reports four-year PAE terms, which are therefore not used in the summary. The 150-day 5000-series update is reported independently by Venable, Covington and DefenseScoop and is kept as attributed. Results of the 180-day budget-reform and university tasks, a 5000-series rewrite, and any PPBE change were not found. FY2027 House provisions come from a War on the Rocks comparison published before House passage, not from bill text; House passage and the failed Senate cloture vote were confirmed on the House Clerk and Senate roll call pages.
